name: Fader blend over 16 bars
lesson:
## Half the speed, same shape

The 8-bar blend stretched to 16: B up across bars 1 to 17, A down over bars 17 to 25. At this length the tracks sit together for a full phrase with both audible, so the blend only works if they were beatmatched and phrase-aligned before you started.

Longer blends are the deep house and progressive default because they let the listener stop noticing there are two tracks. The trade is exposure: any drift, any clashing key, is on show for 30 seconds. Cut B's low EQ before you start if the basses fight; this drill leaves EQ alone so you can hear the fader on its own.

tracks.cue: Gravity's stripped outro runs long enough for a 16-bar blend and then some. Start the drill two phrases before the end of A.
Cue B at its first kick: the pad-and-drum intro sits under Gravity for a full phrase without fighting it, which is the point of the 16-bar blend.
